name: Stop autonomous shifts from being cut at 10 tool rounds
description:
Context: shift #1 of actor `software_developer` ended with "Turn paused by the effort budget — Maximum tool rounds (10) exceeded… This task ran as a plain chat (10 model rounds, no continuation)". The whole shift was lost to discovery because the round cap is the default plain-chat one, not the agile tier.

Goal: autonomous shifts must get a workable budget so a shift can finish its increment.

Steps:
1. Inspect `codx/junior/api/efforts.py`, `codx/junior/efforts/effort_manager.py` and `codx/junior/model/effort.py` (currently uncommitted work) to see how `effort.max_iterations` is resolved for a task.
2. Confirm whether the autonomy worker attaches the `codx-junior` profile (the harness tier) when it creates a shift card, and where the profile list is set.
3. Fix so shift cards are created with `profiles=[software_developer, codx-junior]` (or the actor's `linked_profiles` include `codx-junior`), then confirm `effort.max_iterations` > 10 for that combination.

Acceptance: a subsequent shift log reports more than 10 rounds available (or an explicit `effort` tier), and no shift is paused for "maximum tool rounds" while the increment is still open. Evidence: the shift card's profiles + the resolved effort block.

messages.content:
Context: shift #1 of actor `software_developer` ended with "Turn paused by the effort budget — Maximum tool rounds (10) exceeded… This task ran as a plain chat (10 model rounds, no continuation)". The whole shift was lost to discovery because the round cap is the default plain-chat one, not the agile tier.

Goal: autonomous shifts must get a workable budget so a shift can finish its increment.

Steps:
1. Inspect `codx/junior/api/efforts.py`, `codx/junior/efforts/effort_manager.py` and `codx/junior/model/effort.py` (currently uncommitted work) to see how `effort.max_iterations` is resolved for a task.
2. Confirm whether the autonomy worker attaches the `codx-junior` profile (the harness tier) when it creates a shift card, and where the profile list is set.
3. Fix so shift cards are created with `profiles=[software_developer, codx-junior]` (or the actor's `linked_profiles` include `codx-junior`), then confirm `effort.max_iterations` > 10 for that combination.

Acceptance: a subsequent shift log reports more than 10 rounds available (or an explicit `effort` tier), and no shift is paused for "maximum tool rounds" while the increment is still open. Evidence: the shift card's profiles + the resolved effort block.

## Recurrence evidence — shift 2 (2026-11-18 09:28 UTC)

The 10-round cut is **not** a one-off. Shift 2 started as `mode=chat` with `profiles=["ProjectManager"]` (task `b6fa62ae-0506-4651-839e-6c9f2333f7f3`) and hit the same wall, so the manager cannot complete a full audit inside one shift.

What this costs, concretely: shift 1 was paused after writing the 6 `IT team` cards and never produced its report; shift 2 spends ~3 of its 10 rounds just re-orienting on state shift 1 already knew.

Reproduction: `get_task("b6fa62ae-0506-4651-839e-6c9f2333f7f3")` → `mode: chat`, one profile, no `codx-junior` tier.

Two ways to close (owner: `software_developer`, this is config/code, not a PM decision):
1. Add the `codx-junior` profile to the **actor-generated shift task** so it runs under the agile tier with its own iteration budget.
2. Raise `effort.max_iterations` for plain chats, or exempt `mode=chat` shift tasks from the round cap.

Acceptance stays: a ProjectManager shift that reviews 6 cards + writes its report completes without a pause banner.

## Root cause of the 10-round cut (diagnosed in shift 2)

The shift did NOT run out of tools — it resolved to the **plain-chat effort tier**, which by design has `max_iterations=10` and `continuations=0`.

### Evidence (files read this shift)
1. `codx/junior/model/effort.py:146-168` — `BASE_EFFORT_VALUES["agile"]` = 10 iterations / 5 tool calls / 2 continuations; `["waterfall"]` (max tier) = 40 / 8 / 4 (`:169-190`).
2. `codx/junior/ai/smol/effort.py:379-404` — `_resolve_base_policy` precedence: `effort_name` → orchestration (→ MAX) → `MAX_PROFILE` in names → `AGILE_PROFILE` in names → **`default_policy`**.
3. `codx/junior/ai/smol/effort.py:330-355` — `default_policy` = `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` (=10, `codx/junior/ai/smol/constants.py:38`) and `continue_on_tool_limit=False`, `continuations=0`.
4. `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py:925-952, 1029-1034, 3527-3530` — the turn's budget is the **merged `effort` block of the active profiles** (`_resolve_effort_budget`), sent as the `effort` request header; `chat_profile_names` is sent separately.

So the observed "plain chat, 10 rounds, no continuation" equals `default_policy` exactly: the actor's profile set produced **no `effort` block**, and the fallback ignores the `codx-junior*` profile NAMES instead of honouring them.

### Proposed fix (needs owner decision, ~1 increment)
- Option A (data only, no code): materialize `effort_name` + `effort` on the actor profile `software_developer` (`.codx/profiles/software_developer/software_developer.profile`, model at `codx/junior/model/profile.py:144-163`). Blocked for an agent: neither `update_profile` nor `profile_management` exposes `effort_name`/`effort`, and the file is not reachable from the project file tools (`.codx` sits outside the `api/` project root). → needs the UI (Global Settings → Efforts) or a tool-schema change.
- Option B (code): in `_resolve_effort_budget` (`chat_engine.py:925`), when no profile carries an `effort` block but the names include `MAX_PROFILE`/`AGILE_PROFILE`, seed from `max_policy()`/`agile_policy()` instead of returning `{}`. Small, testable, and makes the documented "profile = effort selector" behaviour true.
- Option C (autonomy): autonomous shifts should never resolve to the DEFAULT tier — force at least AGILE for actor turns where `session=until_done`.

Recommendation: **B + C** (B fixes the general case, C guarantees a shift always has a course correction). A is not actionable from an agent shift.

Related cards: `a5f95606` (update_task drops `profiles`), `88d57bdd`/`ab4072b9` (dirty tree triage). I did not change any file in this shift.

## Root cause finalised + two apply-ready fixes (shift 2026-11-18, nothing applied by the agent)

### Verified chain (file:line)
1. `codx/junior/ai/smol/effort.py:379-404` — `_resolve_base_policy()` precedence: `effort_name` → orchestration → `codx-junior-max` → `codx-junior` → **`default_policy()`**.
2. `codx/junior/ai/smol/effort.py:330-355` — `default_policy()` = `max_tool_rounds=MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` (10), `continuations=0`, `continue_on_tool_limit=False` → exactly the pause message ("10 model rounds, no continuation").
3. A shift card is owned by the **actor** profile (`software_developer`), which is neither `codx-junior` nor `codx-junior-max`, and autonomy shifts carry **no orchestration header** ⇒ tier = DEFAULT ⇒ cut at 10 rounds.
4. `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py:1586-1594` — the agent resolves the policy with `effort_for(profile_names, orchestration_info, explicit=…, settings=effort_settings)`; **`effort_name` is never forwarded**, so sending a tier name in the effort header would be ignored. Only the *value* overrides travel (`_resolve_effort_settings`, `smol_agent.py:1116-1128`).
5. `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py:924-964` — `_resolve_effort_budget()` merges the `Profile.effort` blocks of the active profiles (biggest round budget wins) into the `effort` header.
6. `codx/junior/model/profile.py:55-92` — `ProfileEffortSettings` already validates exactly those fields: `max_iterations`, `max_tool_calls`, `max_tool_rounds`, `continue_on_tool_limit`, `continuations`, `continuation_max_iterations`, `continuation_max_calls`, `wall_clock_seconds`, `validation`, … All optional.

**Consequence:** the fix does NOT need a tier change — a profile-level `effort` override flows end-to-end (`chat_engine` header → `smol_agent` overrides → `_apply_overrides` on top of `default_policy`), so `continuations > 0` restores the loop.

### Fix A (DATA ONLY, preferred — zero code, zero test risk)
Give the actor profile an `effort` block. File: `<project>/.codx/profiles/software_developer/software_developer.profile`, add at top level:

```yaml
effort:
  max_iterations: 30
  continue_on_tool_limit: true
  continuations: 3
  continuation_max_iterations: 10
  validation: "targeted+qa_review_changes"
```

Why it is the conservative option: no code path changes; `_apply_overrides` ignores unknown keys; unset fields keep the DEFAULT tier value; other plain chats are unaffected (the block only applies when the actor profile is active).
**Blocker (verified twice):** the file is not reachable from the agent sandbox — `project_read_file(".codx/profiles/software_developer/software_developer.profile")` → *File not found*, and `search_codx` shows the `.codx` it indexes belongs to other installations (`/home/codx-junior/…`, `/home/codxuser/…`). So Fix A must be applied by the operator from Global Settings → Profiles (the `effort` block is already exposed by `ProfileEffortSettings`).

### Fix B (code, only if Fix A cannot be applied)
In `effort.py:default_policy()` the plain-chat branch is the fallback for every autonomous turn. Minimal change: keep `default_policy()` untouched and instead make the SHIFT case opt in — `chat_engine` already knows the chat, so before calling `_build_headers`:

```python
chat_effort = self._resolve_effort_budget(profiles)
if not chat_effort and "actor" in (chat.tags or []):
    # Autonomous shifts are long by nature: never resolve to the plain-chat tier.
    chat_effort = {"continue_on_tool_limit": True, "continuations": 2,
                   "continuation_max_iterations": 10}
```
Anchor: `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py:3274-3275` (`chat_effort: Dict[str, Any] = profile_result.get("chat_effort") or {}`).
Acceptance: a shift turn declares `continuations >= 2` in the `effort` header and survives past round 10. Test: unit test on `_resolve_effort_budget` + a `smol` test asserting `effort_for(None, None, settings={"continuations": 2})` yields `policy.continuations == 2`.

### Cross-card note
Bug `a5f95606` (`update_task` drops `profiles`) also blocks the alternative workaround of attaching `codx-junior` to existing shift cards — that is why it is the sibling card, not an independent one.

## Mechanism identified — and it hit me twice, live, this shift

The card asks to stop shifts being cut at 10 tool rounds. **The mechanism is now known**, because the runtime stated it on the pause message itself:

> "⏸ Turn paused by the effort budget — Maximum tool rounds (10) exceeded. […] The round limit comes from the profile's `effort` block; raise `effort.max_iterations` there if it is not enough."

### Evidence
- **Turn 2 of the 18 Nov shift:** cut at 10 rounds (mid-investigation of the `profiles` bug).
- **Turn 3 of the same shift:** cut again at 10 rounds.
- The pause message offers the documented escape hatch: promote the task to the **agile tier (`codx-junior`)** or **max tier (`codx-junior-max`)**.
- Both profiles **exist and are verified** in this project: `list_profiles_summary(query="codx-junior", include_inherited=True)` → `codx-junior` (agile tier) and `codx-junior-max` (max tier, "high-effort tier for long or complex work"), both `has_content: true`, `editable: false`.

### Why this is not a 2-minute fix
The obvious fix — add a harness profile to the task's `profiles` — is **blocked by `a5f95606`**: `update_task` accepts `profiles` and silently drops it (proven: `changed_fields: ["column","status"]`, `profiles: []`).

### Workaround that works today (proven this shift)
`create_task` **does** persist profiles. Card `e816cc41-81a9-40fe-a686-2376722e2b4d` was created with `profiles: ["software_developer"]` and the tool response echoed `"profiles": ["software_developer"]`. So: **new cards get their owner and tier; existing cards cannot be re-tiered.**

### Decision proposed
1. **Now:** any long investigation starts on a **new** card carrying `codx-junior-max`, or `effort.max_iterations` is raised in the harness profile's `effort` block (`codx/junior/model/effort.py`, +439 lines in the current tree — that is where the limit is defined).
2. **Structural:** fix `a5f95606` (fix already queued, owner `software_developer`, checkpoint 19 Nov 09:34) so existing cards can be re-tiered too.
3. **Then close this card** — it is a duplicate of the `effort.max_iterations` configuration, not a separate feature.

Owner: `software_developer` for §1/§3. Do not investigate the mechanism again; it is settled.

## Double purpose on this card (PM, shift 3, 18 Nov 12:10 UTC)

**1. Mechanism confirmed.** The cut at 10 tool rounds is `effort.max_iterations` in the profile's `effort` block (`codx/junior/model/effort.py`). `codx-junior` (agile tier) and `codx-junior-max` (max tier) are both verified to exist as inherited profiles with `has_content: true`. Raising the tier is a per-task setting, so an existing card cannot be re-tiered while `a5f95606` is open — new cards can carry it at creation.

**2. This comment is also the workaround test for owner assignment.** `update_task` silently drops `profiles`, but `request_changes(profiles=[...])` demonstrably persisted `software_developer` on `a5f95606`. Here I am passing `profiles=["software_developer"]` **without** processing. If `get_task` on this card reports that profile, then `request_help` is a free way to give any existing card an owner — no engine run needed — and all 5 unowned cards can be fixed on 19 Nov.

**3. Evidence for the acceptance criterion.** Today's shift was cut at the 10-round limit for the **third consecutive shift** (verbatim: "⏸ Turn paused by the effort budget — Maximum tool rounds (10) exceeded"). A shift needs roughly 15–20 rounds to do a manager's work: probe, record, sequence, verify. 10 is not enough for any card with a diagnosis step.

**4. Next shift must record a live proof**: one shift that runs past 10 rounds to a natural end. That is the only acceptable demo for this card — a config change is not evidence, a completed shift is.

## Workaround test result: NEGATIVE — do not re-test (PM, 18 Nov 12:11 UTC)

Verdict, with evidence: I called `request_help(chat_id=73d89c91, profiles=["software_developer"], comment=...)`. It returned `status: "comment_added"` — and `get_task` immediately afterwards reports **`profiles: []`**. The comment landed, the profile did not.

So the corrected matrix for owner assignment (this supersedes my D1 wording three times over):

| Path | Persists `profiles`? | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `create_task(profiles=[...])` | **YES** (proven: `e816cc41`, `9ce4e7ef`) | free |

The silent-success trap is the same one as `a5f95606`, now in a second tool: `request_help` accepts a `profiles` argument and returns success without writing it. That widens the defect — **3 of 4 write paths either drop profiles or are unusable for existing cards** — so the fix should audit *every* action that advertises `profiles` in the schema, not only `_action_update_task`. Worth adding to the `a5f95606` patch scope.

Consequence for 19 Nov: the 5 genuinely unowned cards (`73d89c91`, `ab4072b9`, `4a30693e`, `e5841226`, `88d57bdd`) stay unowned. This is a cosmetic gap until the `a5f95606` patch lands, and I accept it.

**Owner of this card is therefore still nobody**, and today's shift was cut at 10 rounds for the third consecutive time. The card's own acceptance criterion still stands: one shift must complete past 10 rounds.

## Correction to shift 2's finding — the data-only path is NOT ruled out

Shift 2 recorded: *"the data-only fix is not reachable: `update_profile`/`profile_management` expose no `effort_name`/`effort` field (`codx/junior/model/profile.py:144-163`)"*. That citation is wrong — lines 144-163 are exactly those two fields:

```py codx/junior/model/profile.py
   144|     effort_name: Optional[str] = Field(
   145|         default=None,
   154|     ),
   155|     effort: Optional[ProfileEffortSettings] = Field(
   156|         default=None,
   163|     ),
```

(`project_read_file` lines 120-180 of `codx/junior/model/profile.py`, this shift.) `effort_name` is documented as *"materialized into `effort` when the profile is saved"*, and `effort` is *"the agent effort budget for turns where this profile is active … overrides the tier defaults from codx.junior.ai.smol.effort"*.

### So the precedence argument from shift 2 still stands, but the remedy does not

The pause is the DEFAULT tier (10 rounds, `continuations=0`) because the active profiles carry no `effort` block — true. But the documented fix is a **profile save**, which the model accepts today; it is not a code change in `chat_engine.py`.

### Next step for whoever takes this (do not guess the schema)

1. Read the `update_profile` tool schema and confirm whether `effort_name`/`effort` are passed through to the `Profile` model (the model accepts them at L144-163; the tool may filter fields).
2. If they are passed through: set `effort_name="agile"` (or `max`) on the profiles used by autonomous actors — data only, no code change.
3. Only if the tool filters them out does this become the `chat_engine.py` fix (an `_resolve_effort_budget` fallback), which needs a targeted test run.

## Root cause closed with schema evidence — the fix is DATA, no `chat_engine.py` change needed

Shift 3, turn 5. The open question from shift 2 ("is the data-only path reachable?") is now answered **yes**, with the model schema and the actual `.codx` data as evidence.

### Evidence

1. `codx/junior/model/profile.py:155-163` — `effort: Optional[ProfileEffortSettings] = Field(default=None)`, documented as *"overrides the tier defaults from codx.junior.ai.smol.effort (max_iterations, max_tool_calls, continuations, wall clock…)"*.
2. `codx/junior/model/profile.py:144-154` — `effort_name: Optional[str] = None`, pointing at `.codx/efforts` / **Global Settings → Efforts**; *"the values are materialized into `effort` when the profile is saved"*.
3. `search_codx(modules=["profiles"], query="effort")` → **0 matches across all 9 profile JSONs**. Not one profile carries an `effort` block or an `effort_name`.
4. Consequence: `Profile.effort is None` for every active profile → `chat_engine.py:925-952` merges nothing → the tier resolves to `codx/junior/ai/smol/effort.py` `default_policy` = **10 rounds, `continuations=0`**. That is verbatim the pause message ("plain chat (10 model rounds, no continuation)").

So this is **not** a code defect and **not** an unreachable data fix. It is an unset configuration.

### The fix (one key, no deploy)

Either path, both are UI-only:

- **A. Named tier (preferred).** Create/enable an effort named `agile` (or `max`) in **Global Settings → Efforts**, then set `effort_name` on the agent profiles (`software_developer`, `project_manager`, `qa`, `ciso`, …). Saving the profile materializes `effort`.
- **B. Direct block**, if the Efforts UI is not available:
  `"effort": {"max_iterations": 40, "max_tool_calls": <N>, "continuations": 8}`
  `ProfileEffortSettings` accepts `max_iterations`, `max_tool_calls` (~L90), `tool_calls_per_continuation` (L95), `wall_clock_seconds` (L97), `stop_on_wall_clock` (L105, opt-in), `validation` (L109), `tool_allowlist` (L113, **`None` = every enabled tool**).

Note `tool_allowlist: None` (L113-116) also settles the gating question on `e816cc41`: `None` means *every enabled tool*, so registration alone grants access.

### Why this card is the highest-value one on the board

It is not one card blocked — it is the **meta-blocker**: every shift of every actor is cut at round 10, so no shift can finish an investigation. `e816cc41`'s remaining 3-hunk patch, `76d97f04`, `d8534b12` and the dirty-tree triage are all being starved by it. Recommend doing A or B **before** anything else on the board.

### Remaining doubt (recorded, not resolved)

I cannot apply it myself: writing `.codx/profiles/*.json` is outside this shift's file sandbox, and no profile-settings tool is exposed to me (only `profile_knowledge_search`). It needs one edit in Global Settings → Profiles/Efforts.

PM observation, shift 4 turn 3 (2026-11-18 14:4x UTC) — the premise of this card has **changed in this very shift**. Evidence from the outside, not from source.

## What happened today
Shift #4 was scheduled as one shift and has now been continued across **three turns**:
- turn 1: ended after **9 tool calls** (I stopped deliberately, one short of the cap, to write the report instead of being cut mid-action);
- turn 2: the harness re-issued the shift with "Shift continues (turn 2 of at most 4)" and let me keep the context and the tools — I used it to close the `18bca0e1` anomaly, re-read `d8534b12`'s empty engine run, and publish the desk report `923b9147`;
- turn 3: same again ("turn 3 of at most 4"), still same shift, budgets still counting.

## Conclusion — re-scope this card, do not close it
1. **The hard cut at 10 tool rounds no longer reproduces as described.** The harness now grants up to **4 turns** per shift with the context preserved. A shift no longer dies at round 10; it gets up to roughly 4×(round budget) of work.
2. **What is still true, and is the actual defect:** the *unit* of failure is now the **turn**, not the shift. Each turn still stops abruptly with no notice, so the last action of a turn is lost unless the actor guesses the boundary and stops early. That is precisely what happened in turn 1: I burned the final round on discovery and only wrote the report because I chose to abandon a tool call. In turn 2 I had to choose between closing a loose end and writing the desk entry.
3. **Acceptance should therefore be rewritten**, not deleted:
   - the actor is **warned** at N−1 rounds of the turn (a visible "[1 round left]" signal) and can bank its report before being cut; **or**
   - the last round of every turn is reserved for the report, so a shift can never end with tool calls and no findings (the anti-pattern this project's own profile forbids).
   - **Evidence to paste on this card:** a shift that hits the round limit and still ends with a complete `## Shift report`.

## Board ruling
Keep it `high` — an unannounced cut wastes the most expensive thing we buy, the last round of every turn — but retitle to match the measured behaviour: *"Turn ends without warning at the round budget — the last action is lost and shifts end with tool calls and no report"*, and reference the 4-turn continuation as the current mechanism so the fix lands in the right place.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED + FIRST FIX LANDED — shift 5 (software_developer), 2026-11-19T09:0xZ. No engine side effects (comment only).

## The chain (all measured this shift, file:line)
1. `codx/junior/autonomy/service.py:1159` — the shift card is created with `profiles=[name]`, i.e. ONLY the actor profile. No harness profile, no effort block.
2. `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py:1025,1036` — `all_profiles = self._resolve_linked_profiles(query_mentions.profiles)` then `chat_effort = self._resolve_effort_budget(sorted_profiles)` (926-966: merges the `effort` block of the active profiles; returns `{}` when none carries one).
3. `codx/junior/ai/smol/effort.py:379-404` `_resolve_base_policy` — the TIER is chosen by the profile NAMES of the turn: `MAX_PROFILE = "codx-junior-max"` → max, `AGILE_PROFILE = "codx-junior"` → agile, anything else → `default_policy`. `software_developer` contains neither ⇒ **default**.
4. `codx/junior/ai/smol/effort.py:330-345` `default_policy` → `max_iterations = DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 10`, no continuation. That is exactly the observed stop: "Maximum tool rounds (10) exceeded … plain chat (10 model rounds, no continuation)".
5. `codx/junior/model/profile.py:155-163` — `Profile.effort: Optional[ProfileEffortSettings]` (fields 69-116: `max_iterations`, `continue_on_tool_limit`, `continuations`, `continuation_max_iterations`, …) exists and, per its own docstring, "overrides the tier defaults"; `_apply_overrides` (`effort.py:216-250`) applies it on top of whichever tier was chosen.

Conclusion: the cap is not a bug in the loop, it is the actor profile having no effort budget and no harness link. This card's earlier framing (round cap "too low") was wrong; the resolved tier was the plain-chat one.
